t: You're in St John's Chapel, inside the White Tower at the Tower of London. Built in 1080, it's the oldest surviving complete chapel from the early Norman period, and the plain stone Norman architecture is part of its charm. It still works as a chapel royal today, overseen by the Canon of the nearby church of St Peter ad Vincula, who is chaplain of the Tower. The name comes from John the Evangelist, traditionally named as the author of the Gospel of John, though Christians have long debated which Johns he may also have been.
